reproduced_at_1e-2.note: Two different regularization conventions were checked (see script docstring).

cov_sample_count_per_head.note: cov_inf/cov_ret pooled within-class covariance per head is estimated from N = n_inf_pairs + n_inf_pairs (correct+wrong) = 1200+1200=2400 samples (inf family) and 1200+1200=2400 samples (ret family), each vs head_dim=256 -> N/d ratio ~9.4x. extract_functional_axis_perhead.py --n-pairs default=600 per dataset key; n_inf_pairs=1200 reflects 2 inference dataset keys concatenated.

conclusion: Sign is stable across the entire sweep for both cosines: cos(theta_mc,v_inf) stays negative and inside the +/-0.0625 null band at every ridge factor [-0.0032,-0.0021] (magnitude actually SHRINKS ~35% toward zero as ridge strengthens, i.e. stronger regularization makes the off-axis/quasi-null result even more clearly null); cos(v_inf,v_ret) stays positive throughout [+0.284,+0.325] but its magnitude GROWS ~14% as ridge strengthens from 1e-3 to 1e-1. So the qualitative story (theta_mc off-axis / v_inf-v_ret aligned) is robust to ridge strength over 2 orders of magnitude. Caveat: the literal ridge=1e-2*mean(diag(cov)) formula does NOT reproduce the canonical -0.003253/+0.283397 to 3 decimals (only theta_vinf is within +/-0.002 of canonical; v_inf_vret is off by +0.0062) -- those canonical numbers came from a DIFFERENT regularization scheme, the eigh-eigenvalue-floor whitening in probe_oq1_functional_angle.py (eps=1e-6 absolute floor, ~1600x weaker than the ridge=1e-2 additive term), reused verbatim by characterize_theta_mc.py. analyze_probe_direction_geometry.py's ridge=1e-2*mean(diag) whiten_M is a DIFFERENT, unrelated computation (an internal sanity check for a separate probe-direction script) whose own docstring says it need not match -0.003 to 3 decimals, only land in the null band.
